Candidates progressed through the lesser grades, demonstrated a virtuous life, and met further requirements before higher admission, regarded as a great honor. According to Wilkinson, they were the source of Eleusis mysteries.

The text also says that their affiliated members used signs and symbols resembling those of Freemasonry.

s: has symbolical lodges Freemasonry is used as a comparison for the Mayan affiliated signs and symbols. The text also says that Zuni sacred orders have secret rites carefully guarded like the secrets of Freemasonry.

l: Zunis, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Zunis are Pueblo Indians of New Mexico with twelve sacred orders, secret societies, priests, and secret rites, whose institutions are described as resembling Freemasonry.

l: Frank H. Cushing, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Frank H. Cushing, a gentleman sent by the Smithsonian Institution to investigate Zuni customs and history, secures adoption into the tribe, learns its language and habits, and reports twelve sacred orders.

l: Zuni sacred orders, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: The Zuni sacred orders comprise twelve orders with their own priests and carefully guarded secret rites, described as having a strange resemblance to Freemasonry.

l: Equatorial Africa, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: has_customs_resembling Yucatan [in many customs of its inhabitants] Equatorial Africa is presented as the region whose inhabitants share many customs with the Mayas. These customs include tooth filing, belief in sorcery, fermented honey-and-bark beverages, grave offerings and sacrifices, abandonment of places associated with death, large drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and protective leopard-skin charms.

l: Maya mural paintings, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Maya mural paintings at Chichen-Itza and elsewhere depict strongly marked African features, Moo in her home and garden, Chaacmol, Aac, Cay, followers, religious symbols, and story scenes; they are presented as evidence for alleged parallels with Egyptian mythology.

l: witchcraft, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Witchcraft is widely believed in by Mayas and their descendants from remote antiquity. Belief leads some, such as a sick man at X-Kanchacan, to attribute illness to spells and reject treatment; in Equatorial Africa, sorcery belief produces fear, suspicion, illness, and many murders.

l: Balche, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: is_a liquor [made from tree bark, honey and water] Balche is a fermented liquor made from the bark of the Balche tree, water, and honey. The Mayas used it in sacred ceremonies from remote antiquity and continued to use it in their rites.

l: African peoples, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: African peoples are described through customs and warfare: they file front teeth, drink honey-, water-, and bark-based beverages, make offerings and sacrifices at graves, abandon homes after repeated deaths, communicate with large drums, and wear charmed leopard skins believed to protect warriors from spears.

l: Du Chaillu, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Du Chaillu is cited as an observer of the customs of Equatorial Africa in his account of the Land of Ashango. His reports concern tooth filing, sorcery, fermented beverages, funerary practices, drums, fetish houses, native dogs, and leopard-skin charms, and the text uses his descriptions to compare African peoples with the Mayas.

l: Egyptian mythology, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Egyptian mythology is characterized as a transformed or mythical version of historical traditions that the author believes originated among the Mayas. The unit specifically compares its stories of Osiris, Isis, Typho, Aroeris, Nephthis, and Thoth with Maya figures, events, symbols, and monuments.

l: Maya migrations, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: Maya migrations move from Mayab into Hindostan, Afghanistan, Ethiopia, the Persian Gulf, Chaldea, Asia Minor, and Egypt, reaching Afghanistan and the Euphrates and spreading Maya names, languages, customs, traditions, religious ideas, and artistic practices.

l: Ake monument, Vestiges of the Mayas, or, Facts tending to prove that Communications and Intimate Relations must have existed, in very remote times, between the inhabitants of Mayab and those of Asia and Africa
s: The Ake monument consists of three immense superposed platforms supporting a structure with thirty-six katun columns. The columns record 5,760 years from the laying of the first stone to the final capping stone, and it may have been completed around the Spanish conquest.

l: Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Rough Diamond is a collection of frontier observations and connected tales of American character, centered on families, inheritance, violence, migration, and war from the early nineteenth-century western and southern frontier through the War Between the States. It opens with the narrator’s travels through Bush Bayou, across the Mississippi, and to Helena for the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck, alongside accounts of Alonzo Phelps’s failed escape from execution and Daymon’s trial, overturned when his supposedly drowned wife appears alive. At Shirt-Tail Bend, Don and Dan Carlo’s wood-yard partnership collapses because Dan wastes money. Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill try to swindle him, but Don fights for the money; Dan later dies, while Don is presumed dead or dying after the Red Stone explodes and is remembered as the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend. The story then follows Tom Fairfield’s three daughters, Roxie, Rose, and Suza, separated after their impoverished father disappears in a snowstorm. Roxie becomes Roxie Daymon and dies of cholera; Rose is used by Brindle Bill and S. S. Simon in their effort to secure the Lasco inheritance, then dies childless of yellow fever. Suza escapes captivity, inherits Aunt Katy Demitt’s property, and later becomes engaged to Don Carlo, who recognizes her as his rescuer from the Red Stone wreck. A second generation centers on the Simon estate. Young Simon, a wealthy but dying planter, becomes engaged to Roxie Daymon’s grown daughter and wills her his estate, worth more than a million dollars. His cousin Cæsar Simon, also called Cole Conway, is identified as an heir by Steve Brindle and hires Gov. Morock to contest Simon’s will. Against a background of expanding cotton, slavery, railroads, and telegraphs, Cæsar serves in General Sterling Price’s army, is wounded at Wilson’s Creek, and is haunted by the number 77 and his treatment of Steve. The war destroys Missouri, Arkansas, and the Simon plantations. At Helena on July 4, 1863, General Holmes’s attack fails; Cæsar falls, ending the Simon male line. After the Southern surrender, Simon land is sold to satisfy judgments, and the remaining figures enter separate postwar lives.

l: the narrator, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: A living man of respectable parentage, educated in a log schoolhouse, he gained early experience navigating western rivers and observing character. Using fancy names and young surveying assistants, he recounts witnessed or traditional events rather than his own history, including a perilous Helena journey and observations of Alonzo Phelps and Daymon's trial.

l: Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Alonzo Phelps, convicted of murder and sentenced to hang in Vicksburg, had committed his first murder in Europe and confessed to hiding Lasco family papers. On the day set for execution, he escaped jail, was pursued, and was shot dead by an officer.

l: Daymon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Daymon, a young laborer and boat hand, conducted boats across Louisville’s falls, abused his wife while intoxicated, and was arrested and tried for allegedly drowning her in Beargrass Creek, pleading not guilty.

l: Roxie Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Roxie Fairfield, also known as Roxie Daymon, is Tom Fairfield’s eldest daughter, a young, intelligent woman of unstained character. Educated briefly each year at a country school, she becomes the heroine of a snowstorm when she keeps her sisters warm and leaves their cabin to find help; Aunt Katy’s party rescues them, and Aunt Fillis Foster later takes her in. Roxie runs away with her lover Daymon, marries him by common law, and helps build a wealthy life in Chicago after leaving Louisville. She has one daughter and dies of cholera, unaware of Susan Lasco’s fate. After her disappearance, she is believed drowned, but appears alive in court after Daymon’s conviction.

l: Mississippi River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Mississippi River is a great river with tributaries, central to steamboat navigation, the wood trade, and travel. In youth, a narrator crosses it at night in a heavily laden canoe through bank-full, turbulent water and driftwood, guided by a cabin light. Along its course, wood-cutters at Carlo wood yard and Shirt-Tail Bend fuel passing boats amid disputes over steam-navigation monopolies. The Brandywine burns after grounding on a deep sand bar, killing passengers. The river region then extends through plantations, cotton cultivation, and slavery.

l: Ohio River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Ohio River is a principal western waterway near a round-log cabin and passing Port William. Its steam navigation helped create new industries, and supporters of free navigation prized its bank for boatmen’s songs and steam engines. A Kentucky-shore explosion sends victims into its waters; later it frames Suza Fairfield’s homecoming.

l: Helena, Arkansas, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Helena, Arkansas, is a point on the west bank of the river, three hundred miles above Vicksburg. Near its former town seat was race ground where Billy Horner and Henry Mooney raced ponies. Fortified by federals with three forts, Helena was attacked by General Holmes’s forces on July 4, 1863.

l: Arkansas, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Arkansas contains the large estate that Steve Brindle says S. S. Simon left to Cæsar Simon. Arkansas is the state where the legal contest over the Simon estate takes place. The unit also states that Steve Brindle served in Price’s army from Arkansas and that the Simon plantations were located there.

l: Louisville, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_located_between Pittsburgh [on the route to New Orleans] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Louisville, Kentucky, was described as a principal point on the early route between Pittsburg and New Orleans. Its falls required boats to employ resident pilots, and the city was the setting of Daymon's murder trial.

l: Beargrass Creek, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: empties_into Ohio River [at the suburbs of Louisville] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Beargrass Creek emptied into the Ohio near the suburbs of Louisville. Daymon's wife was believed to have been drowned there after her shoe and an unidentified woman's body were found along its margin, though she later appeared alive.

l: New Orleans, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: New Orleans is the destination of the pleasure trip taken by Roxie Daymon and the young people from Chicago. Young Simon and cousin Cæsar also travel there before continuing toward the West Indies.

l: THE ROUGH DIAMOND, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Rough Diamond is a work representing America as a New World and its frontier, pioneer past; in its opening introduction, it preserves pride in log-cabin beginnings and the character formed before later magnificence.

l: the race between Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Near Helena, Arkansas, Silver Heels and the Spotted Buck contest a quarter-mile race for one hundred dollars. The Spotted Buck wins, though observers say jockeying decided it and Silver Heels was faster.

l: Alonzo Phelps's execution, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_scheduled_for the day of the narrator's observation [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Alonzo Phelps's execution was scheduled to take place by hanging on the day he escaped from jail. He did not hang; he was killed by a rifle shot while fleeing from the jail.

l: the confession of Alonzo Phelps, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Alonzo Phelps’s confession ends the day before his execution by declaring that he will not hang. It recounts his first murder in Europe, describes placing the victim’s body atop a coffin in a newly made grave, and leads to discovery of papers taken from the victim.

l: Daymon's murder trial, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Daymon’s first-degree murder trial centers on evidence identifying a Beargrass Creek body and clothing as his wife’s; after court-appointed counsel and a guilty jury verdict, his wife enters alive.

l: Daymon's wife's disappearance, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: concerns Daymon's wife [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] Daymon's wife's disappearance caused great excitement in the neighborhood near Beargrass Creek. Searchers found a shoe believed to be hers and later a woman's body, prompting suspicion against Daymon and leading to his arrest.

l: Daymon's wife's apparent drowning, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_alleged_to_occur_in Beargrass Creek [based on circumstantial evidence] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] The apparent drowning was inferred from the discovery of Daymon's wife's shoe on the margin of Beargrass Creek and a woman's body in the creek. The body was badly damaged by fish and could not be recognized by its face, but witnesses identified its dress as one made for Daymon's wife; the conclusion was disproved when she appeared alive.

l: steam navigation, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a fixed fact [by the period described] Steam navigation on the western waters is presented as a new era that creates unforeseen industries, including the sale of cordwood to steamboats. The Enterprise is said to have been the first steamboat to ascend the Mississippi River, while the Washington is connected with the legal challenge to exclusive claims over western steam navigation. The Supreme Court of the United States denied the monopolist's exclusive pretensions.

l: the American frontier and pioneer past, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_represented_by Rough Diamond [the country a hundred years earlier] [Ill 0020] SCENE FIRST--INTRODUCTION.] The unit portrays the American frontier and pioneer past through log-school education, early settlement, river navigation, flatboats, keelboats, frontier travel, rough local communities, and dangers from animals and waterways. The narrator treats this earlier period as a formative part of American character and says the log cabin should remain dear to the American heart.

l: Don Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Don Carlo is Dan Carlo's brother and equal partner in the wood business, paying its expenses while Dan receives half the money. Associated with the Carlo wood yard, he supports the party seeking to improve society and is its silent spirit. After reading about Alonzo Phelps, he enters headquarters through a chimney, takes gambling-table money, defeats Brindle Bill, and becomes the Hero of Shirt-Tail Bend. Following the Red Stone explosion, papers from his pocket identify him as a recovered dead man, yet he survives after Suza Fairfield rescues him. He buys a small Kentucky farm, remains a bachelor, recognizes Suza at a camp meeting, courts her, and rides with her toward Port William.

l: Dan Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Dan Carlo, Don Carlo's brother and equal wood-business partner, receives half the sales money but spends it and repeatedly fails to reform. As Shirt-Tail Bend improves, he feels out of place. He goes to headquarters with Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill amid plans to swindle him, then is found dead in a saloon.

l: Brindle Bill, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Brindle Bill is a five-foot-eight, square-shouldered man, strong as a buffalo, a little-working wood-chopper, former three-card-monte gambler, and bully of the settlement. A floating-population member raised in Port William, he leads the party favoring degradation and is Dan Carlo’s fast friend, yet joins a scheme against him. After fighting Don Carlo and leaving the new settlement, he conspires over the Lasco inheritance, pressures S. S. Simon, and is imprisoned for Lasco inheritance fraud.

l: S. S. Simon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: S. S. Simon is a wood-yard proprietor, neighborhood planter, husband of Rose Simon Fairfield, and father of Young Simon. He helps Brindle Bill establish Rose’s Lasco inheritance claim through false testimony, takes control of the money, and uses Rose’s share to become a keen financier, acquire four thousand acres and more than six hundred slaves, and build a costly residence. A hard master who works relentlessly for wealth, he dies of swamp fever, deliriously calling for Roxie Daymon.

l: Simon's wife, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a_leading_spirit_of the other party [the party seeking to improve society] Simon's wife recognizes that trouble is coming when Don Carlo goes toward headquarters. She secretly follows with a firebrand and sets the cane pile against the cabin ablaze when she hears the fight. She then drags her husband away and cries out in shame.

l: Susan Lasco, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Susan Lasco, daughter of an English gardener and sister of John A. Lasco, emigrated with her father and later married Tom Fairfield. Her inheritance was a cart-load of gourds, though she and Tom hoped important papers would recover a family fortune. She became mother to Rose Simon Fairfield and other daughters, inherited John’s bequest with her descendants, experienced the jerks at a New Lights meeting, and died beside Tom in their cabin after a cold winter evening.

l: the wood-cutters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The wood-cutters are neighborhood representatives who supply passing steamboats with wood. Ranging from men of sterling integrity to floating drinkers and card players, they settle personal quarrels under early boatmen's law through supervised unarmed contests.

l: the Red Stone, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a steamboat The Red Stone is connected with the wreck in which Don Carlo was left senseless after an explosion. Suza Fairfield is later identified as the young woman who pulled Don Carlo from the river after the accident.

l: steamboats, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: carry twenty-four cords of wood [at one landing, after improvements] Steamboats drive the wood trade on the Ohio and Mississippi rivers, with some taking on twenty-four cords of wood at one landing. Their calls for wood after dark cause woodmen to rush from their cabins with torches, giving Shirt-Tail Bend its name. The Red Stone later explodes while landing on the Kentucky shore, killing and injuring many people.

l: the Carlo wood yard, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Carlo wood yard, jointly owned and equally operated by Don Carlo and Dan Carlo, sees a large wood sale; Dan leaves for headquarters, and Don remains to confront them.

l: Shirt-Tail Bend, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Shirt-Tail Bend is a Mississippi River locality, named for woodmen who ran out in shirt-tails to supply steamboats at night. Initially settled by wood-cutters, it has wood yards, Sundown Hill cabin, and no schoolhouse, church, or post-office. It is associated with Don Carlo, S. S. Simon, and Brindle Bill. After Don Carlo's victory, planters arrive, Simon becomes prominent, and small towns develop.

l: headquarters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Headquarters is an old abandoned cabin at the edge of a small cane-brake, distant from the river. Used by Brindle Bill and others for gambling, drinking, cards, and a scheme against Dan, it holds the jug, admits Don Carlo through the chimney, and is later burned by Simon’s wife.

l: the wood business, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a principal source of revenue [in Shirt-Tail Bend] The wood business is the principal source of revenue at Shirt-Tail Bend, and large quantities of cord or steam wood are sold to passing steamboats. Don and Dan Carlo operate as equal partners, but Don pays the expenses while Dan takes half the proceeds and spends them. The business brings thousands of dollars into the Bend without initially producing broader improvements.

l: the gambling scheme against Dan Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a scheme to swindle Dan Carlo [planned at headquarters] S. S. Simon, Sundown Hill, and Brindle Bill are described as banding together at headquarters to swindle Dan Carlo after a large sale of wood. Simon's wife warns that Dan's money will go that night. Don interrupts the scheme by entering the cabin and raking the money from the table.

l: the fight between Don Carlo and Brindle Bill, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a physical contest [settled according to the early boatmen's law] Brindle Bill starts the fight after claiming the gambling money and saying that Don Carlo has insulted him. Brindle Bill is stronger, but Don is more active and fights with true pluck. The fight ends when Simon's wife sets fire to headquarters, and Don retains the money.

l: the fire at headquarters, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_caused_by Simon's wife [to end the fight and force the men outside] Simon's wife starts the fire by applying a firebrand to the cane pile against the west end of headquarters. A strong west breeze carries the flames over the cabin roof, forcing the men outside. The fire ends the fight between Don Carlo and Brindle Bill.

l: Red Stone explosion, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Red Stone explosion, a steamboat disaster, leaves Don Carlo severely stunned and injured, then leads to his rescue from the wreck while returning home.

l: Don Carlo's money, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_taken_from the gambling scheme against Dan Carlo [Don Carlo raked it from the table] Don Carlo's money is taken from the gambling table after he enters headquarters through the chimney. Brindle Bill claims it, but Don's fight with him and the fire at headquarters end the dispute. Don Carlo is said to have been justly entitled to the money.

l: the half-way castle, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The half-way castle is an early brick house on the southern bank of the Ohio River, about halfway between Louisville and Cincinnati. Don Carlo is left there in a severely stunned but nonfatal condition after the Red Stone accident.

l: Tom Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Tom Fairfield was a Virginia descendant who ran away from home at twelve and settled near Boone Station in Kentucky. Able to read and write, he was restless, industrious but inconsistent, and tried writing, planting, boatman’s work, and preaching. He was popular at wedding parties, raced his fleet horse for corn whisky, married Susan Lasco, and fathered Rose Simon Fairfield and two other daughters. Through his wife he received gourds and built a cabin on land under the Henderson claim, but his family experienced poverty. After his wife’s attack of the jerks, he abandoned church meetings; after her death and the loss of his claim, whisky increasingly dominated his life. He was presumed frozen and buried under snow.

l: Rose Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Rose Fairfield, also called Rose Simon Fairfield, is Tom Fairfield and Susan Lasco’s daughter. During separation from her family, she cares for baby Suza in a cold cabin, is rescued with Roxie and Suza, and becomes Mrs. Evaline Estep’s foster daughter before Estep adopts her after her parents die. Identified through a breast-pin and marriage certificate, she inherits the Lasco estate, then dies childless and intestate of yellow fever returning from New Orleans.

l: Suza Fairfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Suza Fairfield, the youngest Fairfield sister, begins as a shivering baby in an unheated cabin and is taken in, raised, and educated by Aunt Katy Demitt until she can leave as a free woman. At eleven, an orphan, she bravely escapes Tom Ditamus after he abducts her, returning through the woods to Port William. She becomes Port William’s belle, attracts suitors but stays with Aunt Katy, meets and rescues Don Carlo from the Red Stone wreck, and is reportedly engaged to him.

l: Aunt Katy Demitt, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Aunt Katy Demitt is a nearest neighbor and first benefactress of the Fairfield sisters, an economical, industrious woman in Port William. After learning of the children’s plight, she orders Joe and Dick to bring them from the cabin, shelters them, claims eleven-year-old Suza in the settlers’ council, and becomes Suza’s foster mother. She supports their household by knitting stockings, keeps private savings and a will, and later reveals that Demitt relations sought Suza’s removal. She confirms that she has bequeathed her possessions to Suza.

l: the early settlers, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The early settlers in Kentucky endured repeated Indian attacks and violent conflict, remained devotedly religious as preachers improved backwoods society, and nearby settlers gathered to decide care for orphaned sisters.

l: the Indians, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: call Kentucky [“The dark and bloody ground”] The Indians used Kentucky as a hunting ground before white settlement and fought among themselves and with white men there. Some Indian bands attacked cabins, killed women and children, and captured or tortured white men. Their conflicts helped give Kentucky the name “the dark and bloody ground.”

l: white men, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: are_in_conflict_with the Indians [in a war of extermination in Kentucky] White men in Kentucky fought the Indians in a prolonged and sometimes exterminating conflict. When captured by Indians, they might be taken to towns in Ohio and burned at the stake or tortured to death.

l: Virginia, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: admits Kentucky [into the Union] Virginia was Tom Fairfield’s birthplace and the place from which he ran away as a boy. Tom hoped to return there and claim an inheritance, although he said Virginia law gave the land estate to the eldest son.

l: Kentucky, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Kentucky, a new-born State admitted into the Union in 1792, lies between the Cumberland Mountains and the Ohio river, with fertile, black, undulating, wooded land. Once called “the dark and bloody ground,” it endured Indian incursions until 1795. During war, it sought peace and remained in the Union, but was invaded on both sides as Cliff Carlo joined Southern armies.

l: Port William, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Port William is the first settlement and a village at the mouth of the Kentucky River, where it meets the Ohio, on Ohio River bottom land. Its landing draws keel boats, boatmen, idle citizens, and whisky sellers, sustaining a corn-whisky trade through groceries and saloons. It is where Rose Simon and her sisters are separated, where Aunt Katy and Suza Fairfield live, and where Suza returns and later rides with Don Carlo.

l: Kentucky River, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: guides Suza Fairfield's escape [toward Port William] Suza Fairfield follows the Kentucky River during her escape because she knows it will lead her to Port William. When the road diverges, she travels through woods and underbrush along the river until she can rejoin the road.

l: the Indian-white conflict in Kentucky, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Indian-white conflict in Kentucky continued after the American Revolutionary War and was described as a war of extermination. Indians attacked isolated cabins and captured white men, while white settlers responded with intense hatred and vengeance. The conflict ended before Tom Fairfield reached manhood.

l: the jerks, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a spasmodic religious phenomenon [chiefly affecting females during church services] The jerks were a spasmodic religious phenomenon that occurred during church services, especially among women. Tom Fairfield’s wife suffered an attack in a meeting of the New Lights, throwing her head and body violently until her combs flew and her hair cracked like a wagon whip. Tom was frightened and never attended a meeting again.

l: poverty, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: affects Tom Fairfield [after the failed land claim and missed crop] Poverty confronted Tom Fairfield and his family after he returned from a long boat trip too late to raise a crop and then endured a cold winter. Tom and his wife sat sadly by the dying fire, hoping that future inheritances might improve their condition. After Tom’s wife died and his land claim failed, poverty left the three daughters without adequate food, fuel, or protection.

l: Tom Fairfield's alcoholism, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: contributes_to Tom Fairfield's death [through intoxication and exposure] Tom Fairfield became too fond of whisky after repeatedly winning bottles in Kentucky wedding races and associating with dissipated boatmen. At Port William he was drinking late at night when Dave Deminish threw him out after he heaved at a glass of spoiled beer. His drinking contributed to the belief that he became intoxicated, froze, and died in the snow.

l: Tom Fairfield's death, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: After Tom Fairfield was expelled from Dave Deminish’s shop, a severe snowstorm began during the night. He failed to return to his cabin, and the settlers concluded that he had frozen to death under the snow, although his body is not shown being found in this unit.

l: the snowstorm, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: has_depth twenty-four inches [of snow] The snowstorm began in the middle of the night after Tom Fairfield left the whisky shop. By morning, twenty-four inches of snow covered the ground, trapping the Fairfield sisters in their cold cabin and making their rescue difficult.

l: the Fairfield sisters' rescue, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_cared_for_by Aunt Katy [after Roxie seeks help] Roxie Fairfield walked through the deep snow to Aunt Katy’s house to seek help for herself, Rose, and Suza. Aunt Katy directed Joe and Dick to bring them back on a wood slide, with Suza wrapped in a blanket in her rocking trough. The children were warmed and later placed with Aunt Katy, Aunt Fillis Foster, and Mrs. Evaline Estep.

l: the cabin, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Tom Fairfield built the cabin for his family on land whose Henderson claim Virginia later set aside. During Tom’s absence, Roxie, Rose, and Suza endured freezing conditions with scant wood and food until Roxie sought help and they were rescued.

l: John A. Lasco, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: John A. Lasco, an English passenger on the Brandywine and Susan Lasco’s older brother, searches America for her for three years. Badly injured in the Brandywine’s burning, he briefly survives, dictates bequests to Susan, her descendants, and his caregiver, then dies.

l: Chicago, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Chicago is a city named for wild onion, called Chikago by Indians. For a quarter of a century it has fewer than one hundred inhabitants. After Daymon moves there, works as a day laborer, and accepts fifteen acres for a debt, its unparalleled growth lets him sell land and become wealthy. Roxie lives among its moneyed aristocracy, where the pleasure party forms and Simon returns before his death. During the war, loyal Chicago is where Roxie discusses the Simon estate with Governor Morock.

l: Brandywine, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Brandywine, a heavily freighted steamboat carrying many passengers, grounds on a deep sand bar and burns late at night, destroying it.

l: family estate (the Lasco family estate), Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Lasco family estate had been held in abeyance because family papers were lost. After the papers are recovered, John A. Lasco sells the property and deposits twenty thousand dollars in a western bank for Susan Lasco and her descendants.

l: Lasco family papers, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: are_hidden_by Alonzo Phelps [before he left the country] The Lasco family papers are recovered after a condemned man, Alonzo Phelps, confesses where he concealed them. John A. Lasco carries papers identifying the bank holding the inheritance, and the papers are entrusted to the woman caring for him to dry and deliver to a respectable lawyer in Memphis.

l: John A. Lasco's bequest, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: has_value twenty thousand dollars [deposited in a western bank] John A. Lasco's bequest gives twenty thousand dollars deposited in a western bank to Susan Lasco and her descendants. He also leaves the one hundred ten dollars in his pocket to the woman of the cabin who cared for him.

l: Susan Lasco's breast-pin, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_inscribed_with Presented to Susan Lasco by her brother, John A. Lasco, 1751 Susan Lasco's breast-pin bears the inscription, "Presented to Susan Lasco by her brother, John A. Lasco, 1751." Rose Simon produces it as evidence of her connection to John A. Lasco.

l: Tom Fairfield and Susan Lasco marriage certificate, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: certifies_marriage_of Tom Fairfield and Susan Lasco The marriage certificate of Tom Fairfield and Susan Lasco had been kept for years in Rose Simon's box of family keepsakes. Rose produces it along with the breast-pin when claiming the Lasco inheritance.

l: burning of the Brandywine, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: During the burning of the Brandywine, the pilot directs the vessel toward the wrong shore, where it grounds on a deep sand bar and burns to the water's edge. Many passengers drown, while others escape on pieces of the wreck.

l: Lasco inheritance fraud, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Lasco inheritance fraud is carried out by Brindle Bill, S. S. Simon, and Sundown Hill: they forge an inheritance claim, falsely identify Rose Simon Fairfield as the sole surviving child, recover twenty thousand dollars from the Lasco estate, then threaten to find her sisters for further payments.

l: yellow fever, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: causes_death_of Rose Simon Fairfield [after her attack in New Orleans] Rose Simon Fairfield is attacked by yellow fever while traveling in New Orleans to select furniture for her new house. She dies on the way home and is buried in Louisiana.

l: Tom Ditamus, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Tom Ditamus, a lazy, cowardly man with a wife, two dirty children, and an ox-drawn covered wagon, agrees to transport Suza Fairfield for ten dollars and captures her for the Demitt relations. Suza escapes while his family sleeps, and he continues traveling after discovering she is gone.

l: Demitt relations, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Demitt relations plot to obtain Aunt Katy's money, believing Suza Fairfield may inherit; they hire Tom Ditamus to take Suza to the Cumberland Mountains and isolate her.

l: Aunt Katy's money, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Aunt Katy's money is the subject of speculation among the Demitt relations. Aunt Katy shows Suza Fairfield five hundred dollars in gold and silver that she has saved through her own work and economy.

l: Aunt Katy's will, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Aunt Katy's will is witnessed by old Ballard and old Father Tearful. It bequeaths all of Aunt Katy's earthly possessions to Suza Fairfield.

l: Suza Fairfield's capture, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Tom Ditamus captures Suza Fairfield in a foggy morning near his camp, threatening her with a gag and placing her in his covered wagon. He takes her south with his wife and children toward the backwoods of the Cumberland Mountains.

l: Suza Fairfield's escape, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Suza Fairfield escapes at night after persuading Tom Ditamus that she hates Aunt Katy and would go anywhere to leave her. She follows the Kentucky River, crosses White's Creek at a ford, rejoins the road, and reaches Aunt Katy's house in Port William by dawn.

l: Don Carlo's rescue, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: A brave young woman rushes into the water and drags Don Carlo's lifeless body to shore after the Red Stone wreck. At the camp meeting, Don learns that the rescuer is Suza Fairfield.

l: camp meeting, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a protracted religious meeting [held in the woods near water] A camp meeting is held near Port William, with preaching, prayer meetings, love feasts, and visitors camping in the woods. Don Carlo attends it hoping to meet the young woman who saved him and there sees Suza Fairfield.

l: Don Carlo and Suza Fairfield's courtship, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: leads_to marriage [as reported by neighborhood talk] Don Carlo is immediately attracted to Suza Fairfield at the camp meeting and learns that she is his rescuer. They ride side by side toward Port William, and the neighborhood says that they are engaged to be married.

l: The Second Generation, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a later generation of characters [scene title] The Second Generation begins after the characters from the preceding part have died or passed from the stage of life. It follows descendants including Young Simon and Cæsar Simon as they confront inheritance, poverty, gambling, and the consequences of family history.

l: Young Simon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Young Simon, the only son of S. S. Simon by a second wife, is a wealthy cotton planter who inherits four thousand acres of plantations, more than six hundred slaves, and an estate worth more than a million dollars. His mother is dead, and he has poor health and little family knowledge. In the last stage of consumption, he travels toward New Orleans and the West Indies for relief, learns Roxie Daymon’s family mystery, becomes engaged to her, returns to Chicago, dictates a will in her favor, and dies shortly afterward.

l: Cæsar Simon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Cæsar Simon, son of S. S. Simon’s brother and raised by two penniless sisters, grows up imaginative, mischievous, and unwilling to work. He leaves Tennessee, becomes a gambler, and learns he is heir to S. S. Simon’s estate. Knowing family circumstances involving Roxie Daymon and Simon, he helps Simon pursue the inheritance dispute, hires Gov. Morock to challenge the will after Simon’s death, and goes to Kentucky for Cliff Carlo’s help. He then leaves for Missouri, joins Price’s army as private number 77, and proves brave and penetrating-minded despite a selfish disposition. Severely wounded at Wilson’s Creek, he is saved by Steve Brindle and a Cherokee Indian. His recurring fear of 77 and his failure to acknowledge Steve in prosperity trouble him. At Helena he recognizes Steve among federal soldiers, falls in battle during the retreat, and becomes the last male link of the Simon family.

l: Cole Conway, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Cæsar Simon, alias Cole Conway in Paducah, partners with Steve Sharp in gambling; after they lose their money, he tells Steve Brindle his true name and family history.

l: Steve Brindle, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Steve Brindle, also called Steve Sharp, describes himself as a come-by-chance, the son of Brindle Bill and Nancy Wade, whose parents were unmarried; his mother was a sister of Sundown Hill. A private in General Pearce’s Arkansas army and a federal soldier, he recognizes Cole Conway as Cæsar Simon and becomes his old comrade. After sharing money and family history, Steve saves Cæsar’s life at Wilson’s Creek with a Cherokee Indian’s help. Cæsar later denies him amid wealth and power; Steve is reported wounded after Elkhorn, with a card alleging Cæsar deserted.

l: Steve Sharp, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Steve Sharp is Cole Conway's gambling partner in Paducah, Kentucky. He later identifies himself as Steve Brindle and exchanges family histories with Conway.

l: Roxie Daymon, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Roxie Daymon, also called Roxie Fairfield, is a near relative of the Simon family and part of its hidden history. During the first year of the war, she lives in Chicago, is reputed rich despite receiving no Simon-estate dividends, and remains loyal to the federal government. She consults Governor Morock about contesting the Simon will and seeking plantation cotton. Later, married to a young mechanic, she lives happily in a cottage and reads The Workman's Saturday Night to forget the past; her possible survival or descendants torment S. S. Simon.

l: Western States, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Western States undergo rapid settlement and progress during the decade from 1840 to 1850. The iron horse and magnetic telegraph are successfully put into operation across them.

l: West and Southwest, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The history of the West and Southwest during the first half of the nineteenth century is described as full of romance and truth stranger than fiction. The region experiences the rise of a moneyed aristocracy and the rapid expansion of cotton cultivation and slavery.

l: the Confederate States of America, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Confederate States of America provide no promised pay or assistance to General Price’s initial Missouri army, which nevertheless takes the field using weapons and supplies gathered from citizens and captured from Federal forces.

l: Paducah, Kentucky, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Paducah, Kentucky, is where Cæsar Simon, using the name Cole Conway, joins Steve Sharp in gambling. After they lose their last money, the two sleep in an old straw shed outside the village.

l: the decade from 1840 to 1850, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The decade from 1840 to 1850 is described as one of the most important periods in the settlement and progress of the Western States. During it, the iron horse and magnetic telegraph begin successful operation across the region.

l: the settlement and progress of the Western States, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a historical development [especially significant from 1840 to 1850] The settlement and progress of the Western States accelerate during the decade from 1840 to 1850. New transportation and communication technologies contribute to this transformation.

l: cotton cultivation, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_concentrated_in Southern States [during the first half of the nineteenth century] Cotton cultivation in the Southern States expands to gigantic proportions during the first half of the nineteenth century. Young Simon becomes a cotton planter through his inheritance.

l: slavery, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Slavery is central to the plantation economy described in the unit. Young Simon inherits more than six hundred slaves, and S. S. Simon's demand for labor leads him to have them summoned before daylight.

l: the iron horse, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_put_into_operation_in Western States [during the decade from 1840 to 1850] The iron horse is identified as one of the great motive powers of modern civilization. It is successfully put into operation across the Western States during the decade from 1840 to 1850.

l: the magnetic telegraph, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_put_into_operation_in Western States [during the decade from 1840 to 1850] The magnetic telegraph is identified with the iron horse as a major force in modern civilization. It is successfully put into operation across the Western States during the decade from 1840 to 1850.

l: the Simon estate, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Simon estate, inherited by Young Simon from S. S. Simon, includes four thousand-acre plantations and more than six hundred slaves and is described as one of Arkansas’s largest. Valued at more than a million dollars, or more than a million and a quarter, it passes after Young Simon’s death to Roxie Daymon. Cousin Cæsar contests the inheritance with others involved, and the plantations and residence are later devastated by fire.

l: the Simon plantations, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: S. S. Simon's four one-thousand-acre plantations organize enslaved labor by an early bell before daylight; President Lincoln's proclamation of freedom abolishes the enslaved people's monetary value, transforming what the plantations contain.

l: the slaves on S. S. Simon's plantations, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The slaves on S. S. Simon's plantations number more than six hundred. They are required to be ready to resume work as soon as they can see each morning.

l: the dream of the steam carriage, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: concerns the steam carriage [dreamed by Cole Conway] In his dream, Cæsar Simon sees a steam carriage, finds gold and a rule containing directions, and travels south with Steve Brindle. The dream includes a speed gauge, a boiler, and a pump-like handle that seems to draw water from the dry road; Brindle interprets it as a sign of Cæsar's inheritance.

l: the steam carriage, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: An imagined light, four-wheeled road vehicle carries six passengers in its passenger box, follows the golden rule, and has a pilot, rear engineer and fireman, brass boiler, and phosphorus-and-tinder heat source.

l: death, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: ends life [as part of the human passage from cradle to grave] Death is presented as a gradual succession in which old people pass away and new people take their places. S. S. Simon dies from swamp fever, and Young Simon follows him after a short life marked by poor health.

l: Roxie Daymon (daughter), Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Roxie Daymon, only daughter of Roxie Fairfield, is raised and educated among Chicago’s moneyed aristocracy and reaches womanhood. After losing every property case, she becomes destitute. Traveling with a pleasure party to New Orleans, she becomes engaged to young Simon and, after his death, inherits his whole estate under his will.

l: Governor Morock, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Governor Morock is a lawyer associated with the Simon will, operating from the law office at No. 77 Strait street and described as fashionable in Chicago. He exploits Roxie Daymon’s destitution by offering, for fifty dollars, to arrange a legal loophole or “shadow” marriage. He writes young Simon’s will for ten dollars, then takes one thousand dollars in advance from Cousin Cæsar to challenge it, seeking further fees. During the war, he promises money and testimony may break the will and tries to obtain cotton through a federal officer, but gains nothing despite spending nearly all of Cæsar’s money. He ultimately retires, or is retired, from law and survives by cheaply selling his bad reputation for dirty work.

l: Cliff Carlo, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Cliff Carlo, oldest son and representative man of the Carlo family descended from Don Carlo and Suza Fairfield, is a prosperous Kentucky farmer and subscriber to THE ROUGH DIAMOND. During the Simon estate dispute, he consults Cousin Cæsar but stays noncommittal because Roxie Daymon is a near relative, writes Governor Morock, then joins the Southern armies and survives the war unharmed.

l: the pleasure party, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: A Chicago pleasure party of young people, including Roxie Daymon and young Simon, agrees to pay Roxie’s expenses, travels by steamer to New Orleans, then returns to Chicago.

l: the Simon will, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Simon will bequeaths Young Simon’s entire estate to Roxie Daymon, dictated to Governor Morock. After Simon’s death, cousin Cæsar contests it through Morock, alleging Simon lacked capacity; Morock proposes using money to arrange testimony about Simon’s mental faculties.

l: the inheritance dispute, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: concerns Young Simon’s estate [over the validity of Young Simon's will] The inheritance dispute begins when cousin Cæsar objects to Roxie Daymon receiving young Simon’s entire estate. Gov. Morock advises Cæsar to challenge the will and accepts one thousand dollars in advance to undertake the case.

l: the pleasure trip to New Orleans, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: A group of young Chicago people arranges an October pleasure trip to New Orleans on the Roman Eagle, where Roxie meets Simon and a mystery about her family arises.

l: Roxie Daymon and Young Simon’s engagement, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Roxie Daymon and young Simon become engaged after the trip and are expected to marry the following spring in Chicago. Simon continues to think of Roxie despite seeing many beautiful women during his travels.

l: Roxie Daymon and Young Simon’s proposed marriage, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The proposed marriage is set for the spring of 1861 in Chicago. It is postponed when Simon returns seriously ill and can no longer stand alone.

l: Young Simon’s death, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Young Simon dies in a Chicago hotel as cousin Cæsar keeps vigil overnight; his remains are prepared and transferred to Arkansas for burial beside his father.

l: poverty and destitution, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: affects Roxie Daymon (daughter) [after the loss of her fortune] Roxie Daymon is told that she has lost everything and is hopelessly destitute and penniless. She replies that her mother was once a poor, penniless girl and that she can endure poverty as well.

l: Roxie Daymon’s family history, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Roxie says that her mother was Roxie Fairfield, an orphan girl raised in Kentucky. Aunt Patsy Perkins told her that her mother had two sisters, Rose and Suza, whom she called poor trash; cousin Cæsar later learns that Roxie is connected to heirs of a twenty-thousand-dollar claim with twenty years of interest against Simon’s estate.

l: General Sterling Price, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: General Sterling Price is a military commander in the war. In Missouri, he leads an improvised Southern army that marches, fights Federals, captures supplies and weapons, advances to Lexington, and retreats south. At Helena, he commands infantry, captures the center fort, shelters men from gunboat shelling, and orders their retreat.

l: the late civil war between the States of the American Union, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The late civil war between the States of the American Union, a civil war arising from two civilizations under one government, deeply affects the characters through service, divided loyalties, deaths, wounds, opportunism, and property destruction. It continues nearly two years after Helena, then ends when depleted, weary Southern soldiers lay down their arms.

l: War Between the States, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_a the late civil war between the States of the American Union The War Between the States begins after the firing on Fort Sumter and the opposing calls to arms in the North and South. It draws Cousin Cæsar, Cliff Carlo, and many others into military service and destroys the Simon plantations.

l: Missouri, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Missouri is a state invaded by federal troops in 1861, becoming the principal theater of General Sterling Price’s first-year campaign as his army marches and fights across it.

l: Springfield, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Springfield is the usual name given to the battle of Oak Hill, where Federal troops under General Lyon fought Confederate forces under Generals McCulloch, Price, and Pearce. Cousin Cæsar is wounded there after General Lyon is killed and the Federals retreat.

l: the federal government, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The federal government calls for five hundred thousand men through Congress, sends forces into Missouri after Fort Sumter, then during the first year will not interfere with loyal men's slaves.

l: the Union, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_opposed_by the Confederate States of America [in the war] The Union loses the border slave States when they withdraw and join the South, except for Kentucky, which remains inactive in the hope of peace. The war then brings Federal military operations into Missouri and other contested regions.

l: the federal army, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The federal army invades Missouri under General Lyon, fights Price’s forces at Springfield and Wilson’s Creek, retreats after Lyon’s death, and occupies fortified Lexington before its capture. Later, it fortifies Helena with about four thousand men, three forts, and a gunboat.

l: Price’s army, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Price’s army is an unpaid, poorly equipped volunteer force of varied people, initially unarmed; about eight thousand bayonet-guns cross the Mississippi after surviving irregular provisions, capturing Federal equipment, and fighting across Missouri.

l: the southern armies, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The southern armies, weary, war-worn, and sadly deficient in numbers at the end of the war, faced fortified Helena; nearly two years after the battle, they laid down their arms and ended the war.

l: the battle of Wilson’s Creek, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The battle of Wilson’s Creek, also called Oak Hill or Springfield, occurs at Springfield on August 10, 1861; Lyon is killed leading a charge, Federals retreat, and Cæsar is wounded.

l: the first year of the war in Missouri, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_unparalleled_in the history of war on this continent [except for an earlier Kentucky Indian or border war] The first year of the war in Missouri is portrayed as an unusually harsh campaign in which Price’s army marches more than eight hundred miles, often lacks food and equipment, and fights frequent engagements. Despite these hardships, the army remains cheerful and is said never to lose a battle on Missouri soil during that year.

l: the 77 superstition, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The 77 superstition troubles Cousin Cæsar after he is assigned the number 77 and later receives a card bearing the same number. He interprets Steve Brindle’s message that Cæsar Simon had deserted as possibly meaning that Steve had 'fallen off' and wanted Cæsar to follow him.

l: three forts at Helena, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The three forts at Helena were defended by the federals. General Price carried the center fort, while Marmaduke and Fagan failed to carry the northern and southern forts.

l: General Holmes, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: General Holmes commands Price's infantry division in a July 4, 1863 attack on fortified Helena with about 4,900 men, but repeated efforts fail to capture remaining federal positions.

l: General Price's division of infantry, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: has_strength about fourteen hundred men General Price's division of infantry numbered about 1,400 men under General Holmes's command. It was assigned to attack the center fort.

l: Fagan's brigade of Arkansas infantry, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: has_strength fifteen hundred men Fagan's brigade of Arkansas infantry numbered about 1,500 men. It was assigned to attack the southern fort but failed.

l: Marmaduke's division of Arkansas and Missouri cavalry, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: has_strength about two thousand Marmaduke's division of Arkansas and Missouri cavalry numbered about 2,000 men. It was assigned to attack the northern fort but failed.

l: the attack on Helena, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: A military attack on fortified Helena by four thousand nine hundred men began at daylight on July 4, 1863; Price succeeded, but Marmaduke and Fagan failed, ending in retreat with heavy losses.

l: Price's men, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: suffers_loss heavy loss [during the retreat] Price's men captured the center position and sheltered themselves as best they could while the gunboat shelled the captured fort. They later retreated under orders with heavy loss.

l: the battle, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The battle took place at Helena on the holiday of American Independence. General Price carried one position, but the other positions held, and the retreat was made under deadly enemy fire.

l: the retreat of Price's men, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The retreat of Price's men was ordered after General Holmes failed to carry the other positions. It was accomplished with heavy loss.

l: the Simon family, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: The Simon family lost its last male-line link when Cæsar Simon fell. After the war, the Simon plantations and the last foot of Simon land were lost through sales.

l: the proclamation of freedom, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: Issued by President Lincoln, it abolished slaves’ monetary value on Simon plantations, knocking dollars and cents out of flesh and blood.

l: President Lincoln, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: President Lincoln issued the proclamation of freedom.

l: the Simon land, Pen Pictures of Eventful Scenes and Struggles of Life
s: is_sold_at the sheriff's sale [to pay judgments, just and unjust] The last foot of the Simon land was sold at sheriff's sale to pay judgments described as just and unjust.
